newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Lafontaine urges pan-European jobs pact.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Lafontaine urges pan-European jobs pact.

text.p: Oscar Lafontaine, head of the German opposition Social Democrats, on Wednesday called for a jobs creation package for all of Europe, saying such a pact would be instrumental to Europe's curreny union.

Speaking at a union organised two-day jobs meeting in Berlin, Lafontaine said labour policies could only be sensibly conducted on a pan-European basis because of the current similar trend in national fiscal policies.

The effort by most European nations to reduce the burden of corporate taxes would inevitably lead to increased taxes elsewhere, for example in the form of direct taxes on wages and in higher social security contributions.
As both these financing means tended to make employing people more expensive, he warned that this would increase the number of jobless still further if unchecked.
Lafontaine also said that a jobs package would have been far more useful than the stability pact designed to ensure lasting fiscal austerity after nations join the currency union.
